overview_pre: This page covers **skin structure and skin typing**: the basis for interpreting lesions, dermoscopy and treatment risk.
kf: Skin layers: **epidermis** (keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells), **dermis** (collagen, vessels, nerves, adnexa) and **subcutis** (fat).
Epidermis renews about every **28 days**: basal → spinous → granular → stratum corneum.
**Fitzpatrick types I–VI** describe burning vs tanning: I always burns, never tans; VI never burns.
Fitzpatrick type predicts sunburn and skin-cancer risk, and risk of pigment change, keloids and procedure complications.
The depth of a process explains colour: superficial pigment looks brown, deep pigment blue-grey (Tyndall).
myths: **"Dark skin doesn't need sun protection"**: risk is lower but not zero; acral melanoma and pigmentation still matter.
patho_lead: Each layer has **its own cells and diseases**, so knowing depth explains what you see.

mech.t: Keratinocytes mature upwards and shed; melanocytes pass pigment to them.
Basement membrane anchors epidermis to dermis (target in pemphigoid).
Collagen and elastin give strength; vessels, nerves, follicles and glands sit here.
Fat lobules separated by septa (panniculitis sites).
mech.cap: Normal skin: epidermis, wavy junction, dermis with follicle, glands, vessels and nerve, and subcutaneous fat.
